text:
marta: Heads-up — canary in usw3 (A10 pool) showing a p99 latency increase ~35% after merge 4890. Throughput steady but KV cache evictions spiked and kernel selector is falling back to the generic path a lot. Putting rollout on hold.

jon: yikes. any CI signal? or is this only in-prod canaries?

marta: CI perf job flagged something on the nightly A10 perf lane earlier today (see ci-bot msg below). But production canaries are where it blew up.

ci-bot: perf-job/usw3-a10-nightly: regression detected for merge/4890 — p99 +12% vs baseline on synthetic prompt-set. Full artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/7592 (perf report attached) :warning:

arjun: I pulled logs from one affected instance: kernel_selector logs show multiple "no optimized kernel match" for L4-Attention microop and then a fallback path that increases per-token CPU. kvmetrics show eviction_rate jumped from ~0.8/s -> 2.6/s.

arjun: quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-01-31T03:12:45Z] kernel_selector: model=redwood-rlhf-v2 chosen=generic_attn_v1 fallback=1 reason=tile_pattern_mismatch
[2026-01-31T03:12:45Z] kvcache: evict_rate=2.63/s working_set=78MB
[2026-01-31T03:12:46Z] scheduler: batch_size=4 -> applied_backpressure queue_depth=22
```

priya: interesting — the "tile_pattern_mismatch" branch is new-ish from the planner changes in 4890. That could explain kernel selection flips under certain sequence-length distributions.

jon: can we reproduce locally? maybe with a short sequence mix that triggers the same planner heuristic?

marta: started a bisect on canary fleet, narrowing to the planner-change commit series. Initial bisect points to commit abc1234 -> bcdef56 (planner heuristics refactor).

arjun: I ran a microbench on A10 (devbox) with the same prompt mix. Reproducer script below:
```bash
# run microperf with simulated mix
./bin/microperf --model redwood-rlhf-v2 --seq-distribution "mix:short:0.6,mid:0.3,long:0.1" --traffic 200/s --record-kvmetrics
```
Outputs show the same kernel fallbacks and kv evict spike when planner picks the new prefill-to-kernel mapping.

priya: two immediate mitigation options: revert the planner refactor (revert PR #4890) or patch the kernel selector to treat the new pattern as eligible for the optimized kernel (fast fix but riskier). Thoughts?

jon: revert sounds safer for rollout unblock. We should still push a patch-on-top to avoid reintroducing issue later.

sre-oncall: Rolling back canary now and holding rollout across regions. Notifying infra to drain a couple nodes for forensics.

marta: opening issue and tagging the bisect results: https://issues.redwood.example/INF-7812 — added logs, microperf artifacts, and bisect pointers. Assigning to @arjun and @priya.

arjun: working on a minimal kernel-selector tolerance patch to accept close-matching tile patterns; will try to land as an experiment behind a feature flag. If that doesn't show improvements in microperf, we'll proceed with the revert.

ci-bot: perf-job/usw3-a10-nightly: triggered rerun on reverted baseline and experimental flag branch for comparison.

jon: nice. add a note to the release ticket to mark 4890 as rollback-candidate and block further canaries until we have a validated fix. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks all — timeline: rollback now, short postmortem draft tomorrow, and aim to either merge patch-flagged or revert by EOD.

priya: ping me if you want extra perf runs on L4/H100 — this looks A10-sensitive but we should validate across hardware.

marta: will do. closing thread once postmortem is attached to INF-7812. :white_check_mark:
